subject: Request for SLA credit and apportionment: Oct 1 partial degradation overlapping maintenance and CDN incident
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@cirruste.ch>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Cirrus Tech Support <support@cirruste.ch>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Request for SLA credit: partial degradation during maintenance + CDN outage

Hi Karthik,

I wanted to open a formal request for SLA credit for the partial degradation we experienced this morning (Oct 1). Our monitoring shows elevated 5xx rates and sustained latency spikes between 08:34 and 09:22 UTC that materially affected our API-backed features. This window overlaps your scheduled maintenance (noted in the system as 08:30–09:30 UTC) and a third-party CDN incident that FastCDN posted about at 08:50 UTC.

What we observed:
- 08:34–08:50 UTC: increased p50/p95 latency, error rate rose to ~1.4%
- 08:50–09:22 UTC: error rate spiked to ~7% during retries/failover

Because the incident spans your maintenance window and a CDN outage, we need clarity on how Redwood apportions outage time vs. exclusions. Our contract (SLA §3.2) says scheduled maintenance is excluded if customers were notified 48 hours in advance — we did not receive any notice on our side. Separately, FastCDN’s incident report (we included the PDF) indicates they were degraded at 08:50.

Please provide:
1) Your calculation that determines whether October’s uptime falls below the 99.95% threshold after exclusions;
2) Which portion (if any) of the 08:34–09:22 window you consider chargeable;
3) Any remediation/credit you will apply if this period is counted toward downtime.

We’ve attached our support log and included FastCDN’s public incident PDF (attached). We’d like to move quickly on this — can you confirm receipt and expected turnaround for an official response?

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Director of Platform Engineering
Cirrus Tech

Attachments: support-log-20261001.zip, fastcdn-incident-20261001.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@cirruste.ch>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 11:30:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Request for SLA credit: partial degradation during maintenance + CDN outage

Elena —

Thanks for the detailed note and the logs. I received the attachments and have triaged with SRE. I’ve looped in Marissa (CS/Billing) to review the contractual side and quantify any credit.

Initial thoughts:
- We have a scheduled maintenance block in our system for 08:30–09:30 UTC; notifications were issued from infra-notify@redwood.com to the technical contacts on your account on 2026-09-29 (we’ll include the delivery/SMTP headers). We’ll validate delivery and resend evidence if needed.
- FastCDN’s public report is relevant; our policy excludes scheduled maintenance from downtime calculations when properly notified, but third-party outages that cause errors outside maintenance may still count. Where incidents overlap, we compute an \"effective downtime\" by attributing latency/error impact to the root cause according to request routing and time slices.

Next steps:
1) Marissa will run the SLA apportionment and share the math.
2) SRE will produce a short timeline mapping requests to backend error sources.
3) We’ll confirm if a credit is applicable and the amount.

Expect an update by end of day tomorrow (Oct 2).

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@cirruste.ch>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 08:45:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Request for SLA credit: partial degradation during maintenance + CDN outage

Elena —

Thanks for the patience. I pulled the raw telemetry and computed the SLA apportionment per the contract (SLA section 4: weighted availability by request volume). Below is the concise math and conclusion. If you’d like the full spreadsheet we can share it via Drive.

Timeline and measurements (UTC):
- 08:34–08:50: p95 latency increase; error fraction across your traffic pool = 1.42% (measured at edge routing tier).
- 08:50–09:22: error fraction spikes to 6.9% coincident with FastCDN incident at 08:50. During 08:50–09:00, 64% of your requests were served from cached edge POPs affected by FastCDN; 36% routed to origin (our runtime), which saw degraded retries but lower error fraction.

Scheduled maintenance notice:
- We sent a scheduled maintenance notice to the account technical contact list on 2026-09-29 at 14:10 UTC from infra-notify@redwood.com. Delivery logs show the message accepted by mail exchanger for elena@cirruste.ch and support@cirruste.ch (we will attach SMTP headers). If you did not receive it, we will investigate your mail filtering. Per the SLA, properly notified maintenance is excluded from downtime calculations.

Apportionment logic applied:
- For overhead where both maintenance and third-party outages overlap, we apportion only the fraction of requests that hit our runtime and were served with error/timeout due to our stack. Since ~36% of requests hit our origin during 08:50–09:22 and our error fraction there averages 1.8% (retries accounted), the portion attributable to Redwood = 0.36 * 1.8% = 0.648% effective error on the overlapping segment.
- Weighted over the monthly request volume, this overlap contributes approximately 0.0027% to the monthly unavailability.

Conclusion:
- After excluding the scheduled maintenance window (per the contract evidence) and apportioning third-party impact as above, October’s computed availability remains above the 99.95% threshold, so no contractual credit is due.

That said — we acknowledge this was a customer-visible disruption and that notice delivery (if it failed) is our telemetry gap. To resolve quickly, we propose a one-time goodwill credit equal to 5% of October’s invoice for Cirrus Tech, conditioned on acceptance by Oct 10 and signature on a simple credit confirmation (DocuSign link included if you accept).

I’ve attached: SMTP delivery headers (maintenance-notice-headers.txt) and the apportionment worksheet (apportionment-oct2026.xlsx).

Please let me know if you want the raw request logs or further breakdown by route.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: maintenance-notice-headers.txt, apportionment-oct2026.xlsx

From: Elena Morales <elena@cirruste.ch>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Aamir Khan <aamir.khan@fastcdn.io>
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 12:00:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Request for SLA credit: partial degradation during maintenance + CDN outage

Marissa —

Thanks for the detailed breakdown. A few points we need to push back on:

1) Notification evidence: we do not see the maintenance notice in our inboxes (we checked spam and filters). If your mail exchanger accepted the message but our relay filtered it downstream, Redwood still holds responsibility to ensure high-touch accounts have alternative notification paths for scheduled maintenance (ticket and in-console banner). We did not see an in-console banner either.

2) Apportionment method: apportioning only by request fraction understates user impact. During 08:50–09:22 our client-side retries and fallbacks amplified the perceived downtime; product teams are measuring user-facing failures much higher than the 0.648% you report. We’re prepared to share our blended telemetry (attached).

3) Goodwill credit: Thank you for the offer. A 5% goodwill credit is smaller than the financial impact because this incident caused feature degradation across two high-value customer cohorts. We are prepared to escalate to procurement if needed.

To move this to closure: please provide the full delivery SMTP headers and a signed commitment to improve multi-channel notification for scheduled maintenance. Also confirm whether Redwood will accept a 15% credit or provide an itemized service makeup (e.g., a month-long trial of Redwood Optimize premium) in lieu of the higher credit.

We have attached our blended client telemetry (cirrus-blended-telemetry-20261001.csv) and the FastCDN public report (fastcdn-incident-20261001.pdf).

Regards,
Elena

Attachments: cirrus-blended-telemetry-20261001.csv, fastcdn-incident-20261001.pdf

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@cirruste.ch>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 03 Oct 2026 09:20:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Request for SLA credit: partial degradation during maintenance + CDN outage

Elena / team —

Following review (legal + finance + CS + SRE), Redwood will take the following steps to close this:

1) We will issue a one-time credit of 10% of the October invoice (greater than Marissa’s initial goodwill offer) as a recognition of the customer-visible impact and the notification delivery ambiguity. The credit will appear on your Nov statement; to accept we ask for a short confirmation (DocuSign link below).

2) Operational commitments:
   - We will add a secondary notification channel (in-console banner + support ticket) for all scheduled maintenance affecting accounts with dedicated or enterprise plans, effective immediately.
   - SRE will conduct a postmortem within 7 days and share action items with Cirrus Tech.

3) Apportionment: we maintain the current technical method for SLA math (weighted by request volume and error fraction) for contractual purposes, but we will include an additional column in the apportionment worksheet showing \"client-perceived impact\" (aggregated from your telemetry) to aid joint root-cause analysis.

Next steps:
- Elena: if you accept the 10% credit, sign here: https://docusign.example.com/ct-credit-20261003 and we’ll issue the credit.
- Marissa: please prepare the credit memo and schedule the postmortem invite with Cirrus SREs.

We appreciate the partnership and want to make sure we close this with clear prevention steps.

—Priyom Das
VP, Finance & Legal Operations
priyom_das@redwood.com
